messages:
Alex Chen: Handoff — I'm taking the night rotation 19:00-03:00 PT. Quick watchlist + notes below. Please ping if you want me to take anything live.

Alex Chen: 1) KV autoscaler noise (kv-consumer). Alert: kv/hpa-flapping. Symptom: multiple scale events in short window -> cold starts -> p99 spikes. If you see > 3 scale events in 10m, mute alert, reopen ticket for follow-up.

Alex Chen: Triage commands:
```
kubectl -n services get hpa kv-consumer -o yaml
kubectl -n services logs deploy/kv-consumer --since=1h | rg "scaling to"
```
Mute if noisy: `/mute-alert kv/hpa-flapping 1h` (ops policy) then create a short task in ops board.

Lia Patel: FYI I restarted the HPA controller on the cluster at 18:20 after one bad loop, left annotation `handed-off-by=lia`. Expect a small bump in events for ~10m.

Alex Chen: 2) rt-swap pool intermittents: p95 spikes when big models load, looks like KV cache GC on long idle sequences. Check node IO and model process mem. If node-3 shows sustained IO wait, consider routing small variant.

Alex Chen: Quick checks:
```
ssh node-3 sudo iostat -x 1 5
ssh node-3 sudo pmap $(pgrep model-server) | tail -n 5
```
To move traffic temporarily: Console -> Routes -> swap-rt -> shift to variant `small` (or run routing API).

Sam Ortiz: deploy-bot reports canary v3.14 to rt-swap completed 18:50. No errors in canary logs but correlated p95 upticks started ~19:05.

deploy-bot: canary deploy v3.14 -> rt-swap completed at 18:50; metric checks OK.

Alex Chen: 3) Synthetic job flaps (latency_p99_increase). If a single-region synthetic fails, don't page immediately — check monitoring -> synthetics -> last run. If multiple regions fail, escalate.

Alex Chen: Triage steps: pull last synthetic run logs, compare to model-serving error logs, and if persistent, failover region: `eu-west-1` is primary fallback tonight.

Maria Gomez: I've added short-runbook notes in the ops wiki (internal) under "oncall/night-watchlist" with command snippets and contact matrix.

Devon Lee: Are we still honoring the temp suppress for low-priority infra alerts? I want to avoid chasing noisy disk-pressure alerts.

Alex Chen: Yes — low-priority infra alerts are muted for the night (see ops board tag `muted-nightly`). Only page for P1/P2 or if user-facing degraded.

Alex Chen: Backup contact: @Devon Lee (primary backup) and @Maria Gomez (pager/ops). If you need me urgently call my mobile.

oncall-bot: @Alex Chen assigned as oncall for rotation until 1772541200.

Alex Chen: Final: watch kv autoscale, rt-swap p95, and synthetics. If you see a repeating flaky alert, annotate the alert with `flaky=true` and short note. I'm online for handover until 19:10 then reachable via slack/phone. :thumbsup:
